title: The Yangpyeong DTR: Korea's Biggest Starbucks, Right on the Han River
html:
If you love coffee and you're looking for a fun half-day trip outside Seoul, The Yangpyeong DTR is worth the ride. It's the biggest Starbucks store in Korea — three floors of glass overlooking the Namhan River (남한강, Namhangang), with its own in-house bakery and a drive-thru lane. It's less famous with foreign tourists than places like Hongdae or Myeongdong, but it's become a popular weekend trip for Koreans, and it's easy enough for a first-time visitor to plan too.

What Makes This Starbucks So Special

Starbucks Korea opened this store on July 24, 2020, to mark the brand's 21st anniversary in Korea, and it's still the chain's largest branch in the country — about 1,290 square meters (roughly the size of a small supermarket) spread across three floors. Almost the whole riverside wall is floor-to-ceiling glass, so wherever you sit, you get a view of the Namhan River right outside. The "DTR" in the name stands for Drive-Thru, because on top of the regular café, there's a drive-thru lane for people who just want to grab a drink without parking.

Photo: The Yangpyeong DTR, via Korea Tourism Organization's official TourAPI data.

Inside: Fresh-Baked Bread and a Three-Floor Layout

This branch was also Starbucks Korea's first "bake-in" store — meaning the bread and pastries are baked fresh in an on-site bakery instead of being delivered from somewhere else, so you can often smell fresh bread as soon as you walk in. Menu basics work exactly like any other Starbucks in Korea (order at the counter or on the Starbucks app, pick up when your name or order number is called), but the bakery case here is bigger and changes more often than a typical branch. With three floors and around 260 seats, it's usually easier to find a table than at a small city-center Starbucks, except on weekend afternoons.

Photo: The Yangpyeong DTR, via Korea Tourism Organization's official TourAPI data.

💡 How locals actually do it: Most Koreans order ahead with the Starbucks Korea app's "Siren Order" mobile ordering feature before they even arrive, so their drink is ready for pickup instead of waiting in a long line — handy here since this store gets very busy on weekends. The app menu is in Korean, but the ordering flow is simple enough to follow with a translation app, or you can just order at the counter in English; staff are used to it.

Hours, Parking, and the Drive-Thru

The café is open Monday to Friday, 9:00–18:00, Saturday, 8:30–21:00, and Sunday, 8:30–20:00, all year round. The drive-thru lane keeps separate hours: 8:00–15:00 on weekdays and 8:00–20:00 on weekends. If you're arriving by taxi or rental car, there's an on-site parking lot with around 98 spaces (a few reserved for visitors with disabilities), and the first two hours are usually free with a small per-minute fee after that. Hours can shift a little by season, so it's worth a quick check on Naver Map or the Starbucks Korea app before you set out.

Photo: The Yangpyeong DTR, via Korea Tourism Organization's official TourAPI data.

How to Get There From Seoul (No Car Needed)

There's no subway station right at the door, but you don't need a car either. The easiest car-free route is the Gyeongui–Jungang Line (경의중앙선) — this is a regular Seoul subway line, so your T-money transit card works the whole way, no separate ticket needed. Ride it to the end of the line at Yangpyeong Station (roughly 1.5 hours from central Seoul stations like Cheongnyangni or Jongno), then take a short taxi from the station — it's only a few minutes' ride into town. If you'd rather skip the transfer math, an intercity bus or a 1-hour drive from Seoul both work too. Either way, double-check your route on a map app like Naver Map before you leave, since taxi availability near the station can be limited late at night.

Photo: The Yangpyeong DTR, via Korea Tourism Organization's official TourAPI data.

meta_description: Korea's biggest Starbucks: river views, fresh-baked bread, drive-thru hours, parking, and how to get there from Seoul.
